title: Heat Pump Rebate Caveat Vanishes Across Chunks
summary: A county memo contains the real rule, but the trigger sentence and the audit qualifier are split into adjacent chunks. The system retrieves the trigger, misses the qualifier, and answers with an over-broad policy claim.
query: Can a homeowner claim the Harbor County heat pump rebate without an energy audit?

dataset.name: Harbor County climate packet
dataset.notes: Synthetic mini-corpus with one policy memo, one public FAQ, one installer guide, one board note, and one press release.

debugChecklist: Check whether the supporting concept requires adjacent clauses that small chunks separated.
Look for a nearby chunk with a qualifier, exception, or footnote that reverses the first chunk.
If the missing clause sits next to the retrieved one, rerun with overlap or a larger parent window.

chunks.label: Memo chunk 1
chunks.text: Section 2 says homeowners reserve a rebate slot by filing Form 14 with a contractor estimate and the project budget.

chunks.label: Memo chunk 2
chunks.text: Projects above $5,000 may begin a Harbor County heat pump rebate request after Form 14 is filed.

chunks.label: Memo chunk 3
chunks.text: Eligibility is not final until an energy audit is attached to the same filing; without the audit, the request remains pending and the rebate cannot be claimed.

chunks.label: Memo chunk 4
chunks.text: Coastal pilot homes below $5,000 may reserve funding before the audit, but the audit is still required before any payout.

chunks.label: FAQ chunk 1
chunks.text: Form 14 starts a rebate request. Coastal pilot homes under $5,000 may upload the audit later if they are only reserving funds.

chunks.label: Guide chunk 1
chunks.text: Most contractors schedule the audit before paperwork so rebate files do not stall in the county queue.

chunks.label: Board note chunk 1
chunks.text: The 2024 rule let all applicants hold a place before the audit. Board members voted to tighten that rule for larger 2025 projects.

chunks.label: Press chunk 1
chunks.text: The county expanded its heat pump incentive ceiling and highlighted faster review times for residents filing digital applications.

answer.text: Yes. Harbor County lets a homeowner start claiming the rebate once Form 14 is filed, and the audit can be added later if needed.

answer.text: Not for standard projects above $5,000. Harbor County lets applicants file Form 14 to start the request, but the rebate cannot be claimed until the energy audit is attached. Only lower-cost coastal pilot homes can delay the audit while reserving funds.
